source.title: Deep Neural Network Learning with Second-Order Optimizers - a Practical Study with a Stochastic Quasi-Gauss-Newton Method
source.authors: C. Thiele; M. Araya-Polo; D. Hohl

record.tranche_reason: Reports MNIST test loss and accuracy for several optimizers and hyperparameter settings, and a separate seismic tomography application. These optimizer comparisons bear on V4, but the paper studies a different application and optimizer (SQGN) from the version’s cited comparisons.
record.gate_note: The MNIST experiment reports test-set loss and accuracy for SGD, SVRG, Adam and SQGN, with learning-rate, batch-size, and variance-reduction comparisons. These are results on natural-label classification, but the study does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, dropout, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples. Tomography results measure regression loss and SSIM rather than the training-test generalization gap.
record.test_reason: The MNIST experiment directly compares held-out performance of Adam and SGD after learning-rate selection, bearing on V4. Adam performs better in this setting. A paired training-test gap is unnecessary to test V4's held-out-performance comparison; the equal-or-better training-performance clause remains untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: SQGN converges on both applications with almost identical hyperparameters, is robust across the tested configurations, and needs variance reduction to reach low losses. Their comparable-or-better assessment concerns optimization results; Adam nevertheless has higher tomography SSIM, SQGN costs more per iteration, and approximately 3% of SQGN experiments required restarting.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a stochastic quasi-Gauss–Newton method with first-order optimizers on MNIST and an industrial tomography task; it does not use the cited optimizer comparison protocols or directly measure train-test generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: MNIST outcomes change with optimizer learning rate, batch size and SQGN variance reduction; tomography reports differences in testing loss and SSIM between Adam and SQGN.

fits_no_version.finding: SQGN's MNIST learning-rate, curvature-sampling and variance-reduction ablations evaluate the proposed optimizer's convergence and robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SQGN can achieve high MNIST accuracy across several configurations, with variance reduction needed for its best reported performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam learning-rate sensitivity and SVRG performance do not independently establish the adaptive-versus-SGD generalization ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-budget optimizer performance depends on learning rate and optimization procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: On tomography, SQGN and Adam have similar testing MSE, while Adam has higher SSIM and lower iteration cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The preferred optimizer on tomography depends on the evaluation metric and computational budget.

record.problems: The paper reports testing metrics but does not report paired training metrics or a generalization-gap measure. Experiments are averaged over five repetitions, but no error bars or significance tests are given. SQGN sometimes becomes stuck or unstable in early iterations; the authors report restarting those runs.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-versus-random-label held-out performance.
Equal or better training performance; momentum SGD and tuned decay schedules; language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; switching optimizers; decoupled weight decay.
An interpretable fixed-data-pass epoch budget across batch sizes, a workload-dependent batch threshold, and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout and its interactions with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: The authors state that SGD and SVRG eventually exceed 97% accuracy with longer training. This qualifies the finite-budget Adam advantage, although no precise duration or final comparison is supplied.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats V4 as requiring a numerical training-test gap. Its primary comparison is held-out performance. No V5 verdict is justified because the batch experiments leave the effective epoch budget unclear. Results are averaged over five runs without numerical uncertainty intervals; reported SQGN results also reflect restarting failed runs.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the threshold for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Only MNIST comparisons among SGD, SVRG, Adam and SQGN are reported. No language benchmarks, broader tuning, Adam-to-SGD switching, or decoupled weight decay comparisons.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and batch-size scaling across workloads.
Dropout comparisons and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Small MNIST CNN after 100 epochs; constant learning rates selected from four candidates; plain SGD without momentum
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 show Adam outperforming SGD: 97.3% versus 95.5% accuracy and 0.088 versus 0.141 testing loss. This reverses the proposed ordering in this limited setting; it does not refute the frequency qualifier 'often'. R7 duplicates R3.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved 97.3% accuracy and 0.088 test loss versus SGD's 95.5% and 0.141, but this comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Test-set metrics vary across optimizer and learning-rate settings, while the paper gives no corresponding training metric from which to assess the claimed training-test gap; reported results therefore only partially address V4 (R1–R15). No labels are assigned to the original-source versions.
